questions.question: Which condition is equivalent to saying that a real matrix R is orthogonal?
questions.choice_B: $R R^T$ is upper triangular

questions.question: What geometric property is preserved by every orthogonal transformation on $\mathbb{R}^n$?
questions.choice_B: Euclidean inner products and the angles between vectors
questions.choice_C: Only the lengths of unit vectors

questions.question: Which of the following is true about the columns of an orthogonal matrix $R \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times n}$?
questions.choice_A: They form a basis but are not necessarily orthonormal
questions.choice_B: They are all eigenvectors with eigenvalue 1
questions.choice_C: They form an orthonormal basis of $\mathbb{R}^n$
questions.choice_D: They must be pairwise orthogonal but can have arbitrary norms

questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes $\mathrm{SO}(n)$ from $\mathrm{O}(n)$?
questions.choice_B: $\mathrm{SO}(n)$ is not a group under matrix multiplication
questions.choice_C: $\mathrm{SO}(n)$ consists of symmetric orthogonal matrices only
questions.choice_D: $\mathrm{SO}(n)$ is the subgroup of $\mathrm{O}(n)$ with determinant $+1$

questions.question: If $R$ is orthogonal, which statement about its inverse is correct?
questions.choice_B: $R^{-1}$ does not exist unless $\det(R)=1$

questions.question: What does the determinant of an orthogonal matrix tell you geometrically?
questions.choice_B: Whether the transformation preserves orientation ($+1$) or reverses it ($-1$)
questions.choice_D: The rotation angle around an axis

questions.question: Which of the following is a characterization of orthogonal transformations in terms of norms?
questions.choice_A: They preserve norms of only a specific subspace
questions.choice_B: They double the norm of every vector
questions.choice_C: They preserve the Euclidean norm of every vector: $\|Rx\|_2 = \|x\|_2$ for all $x$

questions.question: Which property is true for the composition of orthogonal matrices $R_1$ and $R_2$?
questions.choice_B: $R_1 R_2$ has determinant zero

questions.question: In $\mathbb{R}^2$, which matrices represent reflections across lines through the origin?
questions.choice_B: Orthogonal matrices with determinant $+1$

questions.question: Which statement about eigenvalues of a real orthogonal matrix $R$ is correct?
questions.choice_A: All eigenvalues are real and positive
questions.choice_B: All eigenvalues lie on the unit circle in the complex plane

questions.question: What is the kernel of the determinant homomorphism $\det: \mathrm{O}(n) \to \{\pm 1\}$?
questions.choice_B: All diagonal orthogonal matrices

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the connectedness of $\mathrm{O}(n)$ and $\mathrm{SO}(n)$ in the standard topology?
questions.choice_B: $\mathrm{SO}(n)$ has two connected components
questions.choice_C: $\mathrm{O}(n)$ has two connected components, while $\mathrm{SO}(n)$ is connected (for $n \ge 2$)
questions.choice_D: Both are disconnected with infinitely many components

questions.question: Which statement about volume is true for orthogonal matrices acting on $\mathbb{R}^n$?
questions.choice_A: They scale volume by $\det(R)$, which is either $+1$ or $-1$ in absolute value
questions.choice_B: They scale volume by the trace of the matrix
questions.choice_C: They collapse volume to zero unless $R=I$
questions.choice_D: They expand volume by a factor of 2

questions.question: Which of the following is an equivalent condition to inner-product preservation by $R$?
questions.choice_A: $\langle Rx, Ry \rangle = \langle x, y \rangle$ for all $x,y$ if and only if $R^T R = I$
questions.choice_B: $\langle Rx, Ry \rangle = 2\langle x, y \rangle$ for all $x,y$
questions.choice_C: $\langle Rx, y \rangle = \langle x, Ry \rangle$ for all $x,y$ if and only if $R$ is symmetric
questions.choice_D: $\langle Rx, Ry \rangle = \langle x, y \rangle$ implies $R$ is diagonal

questions.question: Which statement is true about the inverse of an orthogonal transformation in geometric terms?
questions.choice_A: It is a projection onto a subspace
questions.choice_B: It is an isometry that undoes the original isometry, equal to the transpose map
questions.choice_C: It scales distances by a constant factor
questions.choice_D: It reflects across the identity matrix

questions.question: In $\mathbb{R}^3$, which of the following transformations is in $\mathrm{SO}(3)$?
questions.choice_A: A rotation about an axis through the origin by some angle
questions.choice_B: Reflection across a plane through the origin

questions.question: Which of the following is always true for an orthogonal matrix $R$?
questions.choice_B: $R$ is normal and diagonalizable over $\mathbb{C}$ with eigenvalues on the unit circle

questions.question: What is the relationship between angle preservation and inner-product preservation for linear maps on $\mathbb{R}^n$?
questions.choice_A: Angle preservation is strictly stronger than inner-product preservation
questions.choice_B: If a linear map preserves angles and norms, it preserves the inner product
questions.choice_C: Angle preservation implies the map is a projection
questions.choice_D: Inner-product preservation does not imply norm preservation

questions.question: Which of the following is true about $\mathrm{O}(n)$ as a group?
questions.choice_A: It is not closed under matrix multiplication
questions.choice_B: Every element has order 2

questions.question: Which construction yields a reflection represented by an orthogonal matrix?
questions.choice_B: Shear $S = I + uv^T$ with $u \ne 0$
questions.choice_D: Projection $P = QQ^T$ with $Q$ having orthonormal columns

questions.question: Which statement correctly links the QR decomposition and orthogonal matrices?
questions.choice_A: In a QR decomposition $A = QR$, $Q$ has orthonormal columns and is orthogonal when $A$ is square
questions.choice_B: In a QR decomposition, $R$ is always orthogonal
questions.choice_C: QR factorization exists only for orthogonal $A$
